questions.q: Which mountain range to the north puts the Duero vineyards of Castilla y León in a rain shadow, by the Court's account?
questions.exp: The Court's Introductory climate cell names the Cantabrian Mountains, which catch the rain off the Bay of Biscay before it reaches the northern meseta. Ribera del Duero gets little more than 450 millimetres a year as a result, and the same range shelters Rioja to the east.

questions.q: Besides the rain shadow, which feature of Castilla y León's continental climate does the Court stress?
questions.exp: The Court describes a continental climate with extreme seasonal and diurnal shifts. On the high plateau a hot August day can be followed by a night some 20 degrees colder, which holds acidity and builds colour and tannin in Tempranillo's skins; the sea is far away and spring frost is a real hazard.

questions.q: What name is given to the high, flat central plateau that carries Ribera del Duero, Rueda and Toro?
questions.exp: The Court's physical feature for Castilla y León is the high altitude meseta, the plateau of central Spain, with vineyards at roughly 700 to 1,000 metres. The montado is Portugal's cork oak savannah, the garrigue the scrub of southern France and the puszta the Hungarian plain.

questions.q: Rueda's fresh whites are based on Verdejo. Which second grape does the Court name for them?
questions.exp: The Court lists Rueda's whites as Verdejo and Sauvignon Blanc. A Rueda Verdejo label needs at least 85 per cent Verdejo and a Rueda Sauvignon at least 85 per cent Sauvignon Blanc; the two share a herbal, citrus register. Albariño is Galician, Parellada Catalan and Hondarrabi Zuri Basque.

questions.q: Tinta de Toro is one of the two names the Court prints for Tempranillo in Castilla y León. What is the other, used in Ribera del Duero?
questions.exp: Ribera del Duero calls Tempranillo Tinta del País or Tinto Fino, and Toro calls it Tinta de Toro, the two synonyms the Court prints. Elsewhere it is Cencibel in La Mancha, Ull de Llebre in Catalonia and Tinta Roriz or Aragonez in Portugal.

questions.q: How does the Court describe the drinking window of the red wines of Bierzo DO?
opts: Enjoyable young or after a few years
Released only after five years, two in oak
Made to be drunk within the year
Closed for a decade before they open
questions.exp: The Court's Certified cell gives Bierzo red wines that can be enjoyed young or aged for a few years: Mencía on the slate slopes of this sheltered basin in the province of León gives floral, red-fruited reds of medium body, fresh enough to drink early and structured enough to keep. Five years with two in oak is the Ribera del Duero Gran Reserva rule, not a description of Bierzo.

questions.q: A Ribera del Duero Reserva tinto ages for three years in all. How much of that time, at the least, must it spend in oak?
questions.exp: The Court gives Ribera del Duero Crianza a minimum of two years including one in oak, Reserva three years including one in oak, and Gran Reserva five years including two in oak. Ribera's barrel minimums are stricter than Spain's national floors, which ask only six months in oak of a Crianza.

questions.q: A Ribera del Duero Gran Reserva tinto must spend at least two years in oak. What minimum total ageing does the Court set for it?
questions.exp: Ribera del Duero Gran Reserva needs at least five years of ageing, two of them in oak, by the Court's Certified cell, the same figures it gives for Rioja. The rest of the time is spent in bottle, and the long release suits the firm tannin of high-altitude Tinto Fino.

questions.q: Martinsancho is the Court's named producer for which Castilian DO?
questions.exp: The Court lists Martinsancho under Rueda: a Verdejo from La Seca, in the heart of the denomination, made from an old family vineyard of the grape. Its other Castilian names are Vega Sicilia, Pesquera and Pingus for Ribera del Duero and Descendientes de J. Palacios for Bierzo.

questions.q: Descendientes de J. Palacios is the Court's named house for which DO of Castilla y León?
questions.exp: The Court lists Descendientes de J. Palacios under Bierzo. Founded in 1999 at Corullón, the estate farms old Mencía on steep slate terraces, with Pétalos as its entry wine and the single vineyard La Faraona at the top; the family's other estates lie in Priorat and Rioja.

questions.q: In which two kinds of oak does the Court say Ribera del Duero reds may be aged?
questions.exp: The Court's Ribera del Duero style runs from young wines for early drinking to long ageing in American or French oak. American oak gives the older coconut and vanilla style; French oak, favoured by many modern estates, gives finer grain and spice to the dark, firm Tinto Fino.
